attack_indicators: presence of suspicious URLs often with uncommon or unrelated domain names
use of urgent or enticing subject lines promising financial gain or health benefits
inclusion of personal or financial solicitation language typical of social engineering
email body containing spelling/grammar errors and unusual formatting
use of generic greetings or no personalization
presence of embedded contact information with suspicious email addresses or fax numbers
attack_signatures: phishing URL pattern: URLs with uncommon TLDs or domain names unrelated to claimed organizations (e.g., http://www.largevalue.net, http://spreadreciprocity.com)
advance-fee scam narrative: long, detailed story involving inheritance, abandoned funds, or bank officials requesting cooperation
medication and health product spam: subject lines and bodies promoting cheap or discreet pharmaceuticals with embedded URLs
use of fake corporate or banking identities with contact details to establish false legitimacy
inclusion of HTML or encoded characters in subject lines to evade simple keyword detection (e.g., =?iso-8859-1?q?next=20of=20kin=2e?=)
insertion of unrelated or nonsensical text blocks to confuse automated filters
technical_markers: URL frequency: malicious emails contain at least one embedded URL linking to suspicious domains
subject length: phishing subjects tend to be short, enticing phrases (average 3-8 words)
body length: phishing emails vary widely but often contain long narratives (>200 words) or short promotional blurbs (<50 words)
presence of numeric or alphanumeric codes in greetings or body (e.g., 'Dear d7676e9cd908474e8bcf5638be1a1af7')
use of non-standard email addresses with spaces or inserted characters (e.g., 'timkennedyo 03 @ netscape . net')
time stamps or dates embedded in body text to create urgency or legitimacy
normal_indicators: benign emails contain formal or informational content such as newsletters, corporate communications, academic calls for papers, or technical discussions
subjects are descriptive and relevant to the body content without sensational language
absence of unsolicited URLs or presence of URLs linking to well-known, reputable domains
email bodies exhibit proper grammar, spelling, and professional formatting
presence of sender/source metadata consistent with known legitimate sources (e.g., Enron, CNN, academic journals)
benign emails often contain structured information like dates, contact info, and references consistent with professional communication
baseline_metrics: subject length: typically longer and descriptive (average 5-15 words)
body length: varies widely but generally coherent and topic-focused (50-1000+ words)
URL presence: benign emails rarely contain URLs or contain URLs to reputable domains
email address formatting: standard format without inserted spaces or unusual characters
absence of suspicious numeric/alphanumeric codes in greetings or body
